sources.title: Andrea A. Hunter, Osage Nation: Osage Cultural History
sources.note: Direct/full indexed tribal historical-preservation synthesis, excerpt from 2013 affiliation report. Oral, linguistic and archaeological arguments are distinguished; precise prehistoric migration years and automatic Oneota identification not adopted.

sources.title: Missouri State Parks: Osage Village State Historic Site
sources.note: Direct site account: eighteenth-century village, excavated house dimensions, gardens, river foods and fur trade. Its broad origin theory is not adopted over current Osage historical-preservation interpretation.

sources.title: Osage Nation Historic Preservation Office: Osage Lodges and Villages Fact Sheet
sources.note: Direct two-page teaching sheet, compiled 2018 from named scholarship and tribal education project. Historical domestic construction, furniture, village divisions. Exact clan counts and generalized marriage rule omitted.

sources.title: Oklahoma Historical Society: Osage Agency records guide
sources.note: Direct archival guide, printed page 28, Land and Realty Division: removal from Kansas, 1872 purchase from Cherokee Nation, title held in trust, 1906 allotment. No unsupported exact day for community migration.

sources.title: Osage Nation: Did You Know? Osage Murders
sources.note: Original full indexed tribal account: 1906 mineral estate and headrights, inheritance motive and 1920s murders. Article assertion that all killings stopped with one arrest is not adopted; no definitive murder total given.

sources.title: Osage Nation: Sugarloaf Mound
sources.note: Direct tribal preservation history: 2009 purchase of summit property, protection and landscape stabilization. Earlier page ownership fraction is not presented as current ownership status.

sources.title: Osage Nation: Holiday Happenings and Ways to Give, 2021
sources.note: Direct original Tree of Gifts heading and bilingual program name, children’s wishes and December 2021 deadline. Exact Osage string copied, including combining nasal mark. Erroneous January 2021 winner date elsewhere on page unused.

sources.title: Michael Everson and colleagues: Proposal to encode the Osage script, 2014
sources.note: Direct original encoding proposal, opening history and community participants. Modern orthography led by Mogri Lookout, not ancient script.

sources.title: Osage Nation: Harvest Land
sources.note: Original full indexed program account, response to 2020 supply disruption and investment in greenhouse, aquaponics and orchard. Historical development only; no claim facilities remain open in September 2026, given recent closure reporting.

sources.title: Osage Nation Constitution, sixth edition, 2024
sources.note: Direct constitutional text: 2006 ratification, preamble and Article V three branches. Used as historical/governmental primary evidence, not a claim resolving disputed external jurisdiction.

sources.title: Eastern Shawnee Tribe of Oklahoma: History
sources.note: Original full indexed tribal account, homeland, seasonal dwellings/ceremonies and distinct present-day nations. Overbroad statement that 1813 ended all united Indigenous resistance and erroneous implication all present recognition dates derive from removal era are not adopted.

sources.title: Kentucky Archaeological Survey: Lower Shawneetown
sources.note: Direct original site account: mid-1730s to 1758 town, diplomacy, Bentley structure and trash disposal assemblages. Finds explicitly tied to mid-eighteenth-century context; no automatic claim every Fort Ancient site is Shawnee.

sources.title: Indiana Department of Natural Resources: Indigenous Peoples in Indiana
sources.note: Direct Prophetstown and Tecumseh sections: 1808 founding, differing Native political strategies, 1811 destruction and 1813 death. Page has erroneous November 11 battle date; day omitted. General Miami-specific domestic claims not transferred to Shawnee.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: Shawnee removal treaty case study
sources.note: Direct primary 1831 treaty excerpts and explanatory presentation; Wapakoneta/Hog Creek communities, land cession and removal promises. Treaty language is a government document, not neutral proof all individuals freely wanted removal.

sources.title: Shawnee Tribe: Manual Labor School opening anniversary, 2021
sources.note: Original full indexed tribal account, October 28, 1839 opening, children resident at Fairway and tribal historical-preservation work. No assertion that unconfirmed burials have been found.

sources.title: Shawnee Tribe: Historic structure report grant announcement, 2022
sources.note: Original indexed tribal press statement including Chief Ben Barnes address; three brick buildings, attic sleeping and field labour. Historical-structure report proposed, not represented as completed.

sources.title: Eastern Shawnee Tribe: Telling Our Stories sources, Chapter 9
sources.note: Full original indexed page checked; direct request fails. Caption names Wyandotte potter Richard Zane Smith and reconstruction used to cook corn/venison. Purpose explicitly includes investigating relationship to Fort Ancient archaeology.

sources.title: University of Missouri-Kansas City Libraries: Shawnee Sun newspaper
sources.note: Original indexed collection exhibit: Jotham Meeker, March 1835 issue, surviving November 1841 sheet. Avoids disputed superlatives and exact current count of all surviving copies.

sources.title: Shawnee Tribe: Messages from the Chiefs, Fall 2024
sources.note: Root substituted directly readable original tribal Fall 2024 message for February PDF whose indexed text could not be reproduced. Roy D. Baldridge heading supplies Hato Caakiwiyeefa and Hello everyone.

sources.title: Shawnee Tribe: Shawnee Language Immersion Program
sources.note: Original full indexed program history, 2020 emergency, virtual classes and first-language specialist George Blanchard, small classes and auditory focus. No stale current enrolment totals asserted.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Living Osage people and nation, with named archaeological/historical examples. No association added to separate osage-oklahoma record in this batch.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Index1492 to 1783; first world-1492 feature1492 to 1500 bbox[-103.8664387,31.0152742,-78.5977860,41.1460487]. Outline is much broader than documented core Missouri/Osage River settlement and extends from southwest toward Appalachians. Explicit public warning; no geometry correction claimed.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Early migration reconstruction attributed, no precise precontact founding event. Later phases visibly separated. Modern Tree of Gifts sample is 2021, modern alphabet explained. Harvest Land described as post-2020 development only, avoiding an unverified claim of current operation.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Broad historical Shawnee peoples narrative, explicitly distinguishing modern Eastern, Absentee and Shawnee Tribe governments. No separate modern reservation or combined Potawatomi-Shawnee IDs absorbed.

batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Lower Shawneetown archaeology mid-eighteenth century; Prophetstown1808, removal treaty1831, school1839, printing1835 and modern writing2024 explicitly separated. Replica pottery is modern and Fort Ancient ethnic affiliation remains an investigation, not a blanket equation.
